open_points.subject: ServiceCredential.expires_at
open_points.text: “a service credential's expires_at — are validated and kept as supplied” conflicts with the formal invariant “an expiry it writes is that instant plus its TTL”
open_points.question: Is a service credential’s optional expires_at the administrator-supplied instant, or must the operation derive it from its single clock instant and a TTL?
options: Keep the administrator-supplied expires_at unchanged
Derive expires_at as operation_now plus a configured TTL
Treat source-supplied expiries as an explicit exception to the formal invariant
open_points.default_guess: Treat ServiceCredential.expires_at as an explicit source-supplied exception and keep it after UTC normalization.

witness.initial: An active service principal has no credential; the clock reads 2026-11-06 10:00 UTC and an administrator requests a credential expiring at 2026-11-07 15:00 UTC.
events: The administrator issues the credential with the requested expires_at.
The operation persists the new ServiceCredential.
outcomes: The credential expires at the supplied 15:00 instant.
The credential expires at operation_now plus an implementer-selected or configured TTL, so the supplied instant is replaced or refused.
witness.observer: The administrator and producer when the credential remains usable after the differing expiry instants.

open_points.subject: Persisted source-supplied timestamps
open_points.text: “Persisted timestamps are UTC, stored as offset-naive datetimes” and “Times a source supplies … are validated and kept as supplied, never replaced by the clock” do not say whether an offset-aware supplied value is preserved or converted to offset-naive UTC.
open_points.question: For a source-supplied timestamp with an offset, must persistence preserve its representation, reject it unless already UTC, or convert its instant to offset-naive UTC?
options: Accept any offset-aware instant and convert it to offset-naive UTC
Accept only UTC-offset-aware input and remove the UTC offset for persistence
Keep the offset-aware value exactly as supplied
Reject every offset-aware value and require offset-naive UTC input
open_points.default_guess: Require an aware instant, convert it to UTC, then persist the same instant as offset-naive UTC.

witness.initial: A producer publishes approved_at as 2026-11-06T11:00:00+01:00, representing 10:00 UTC.
events: The authenticated producer imports an otherwise valid snapshot.
outcomes: approved_at is kept exactly as supplied with +01:00, or the import is rejected because the persisted form must be offset-naive.
witness.observer: A later snapshot reader or fingerprint/replay classifier.

open_points.subject: Validation of source-supplied times
open_points.text: “Times a source supplies … are validated and kept as supplied” names no validation rules for approved_at, published_at, confirmed_at, document_date, photo_date, payment_date, or ServiceCredential.expires_at.
open_points.question: Which temporal conditions make each source-supplied time invalid—for example missing timezone, non-UTC offset, future value, past credential expiry, or inconsistent ordering between approved_at and published_at?
options: Validate only type and UTC representability
Also reject source event times later than the operation clock
Apply field-specific ordering and past/future constraints
Accept already decoded values without semantic time validation
open_points.default_guess: Validate type and UTC representability only, except reject a credential expires_at that is not strictly after operation_now.

witness.initial: At operation_now 2026-11-06 10:00 UTC, an administrator requests a service credential with expires_at 09:00 UTC that day.
events: The administrator submits the otherwise valid issuance request.
outcomes: The credential is accepted and persisted already expired.
The issuance is refused because expires_at is not strictly after operation_now.
witness.observer: The administrator receiving success or refusal.

open_points.subject: Meaning and propagation of an operation’s single clock instant
open_points.text: “An operation reads the clock once for its own timestamps … and every current-time comparison” does not define whether “operation” is the HTTP request, the owning use case, each called module, or each transaction.
open_points.question: When one request calls authentication/authorization and then a domain use case, must every layer receive one shared now value, or may each called operation read its own clock once?
options: One instant for the entire public request and all nested work except audit_writer
One instant per owning use case, allowing authentication and domain work to use different instants
One instant per transaction or module call
open_points.default_guess: Capture one instant at the owning public use-case boundary and pass it through authentication, authorization, comparisons, and writes; allow only audit_writer its stated separate read.

witness.initial: A valid staff session expires at 10:00:00.500 UTC; request handling begins at 10:00:00.400 UTC.
events: The route then invokes a mutation use case at 10:00:00.600 UTC.
outcomes: A request-wide instant of 10:00:00.400 is used, so authentication and the mutation proceed.
Session resolution and the mutation use separate instants; the later check sees the session expired and refuses the mutation.
witness.observer: The staff caller, who sees success or authentication refusal.

open_points.subject: Clock capture point
open_points.text: “An operation reads the clock once” does not state at what point in the operation that read occurs.
open_points.question: Is now captured at operation entry, after request decoding, after records are loaded, immediately before validity checks, or when the transaction begins?
options: Capture at the first instruction of the owning operation
Capture after decoding but before authentication and repository reads
Capture immediately before the first time comparison or timestamped write
Capture when the transaction begins
open_points.default_guess: Capture after input decoding and immediately before authentication/transactional work begins.

witness.initial: A session expires at 10:00:01.000 UTC; request decoding starts at 10:00:00.900 and finishes at 10:00:01.100.
events: A staff caller submits a valid project mutation just before expiry.
The operation performs its single permitted clock read.
outcomes: Reading at operation/request entry yields now before expiry, so the session is usable.
Reading after decoding yields now at or after expiry, so the request is refused.

open_points.subject: Offset-aware timestamps encountered in persistence
open_points.text: “Reading … an offset-aware persisted timestamp … [is] forbidden” does not specify how a repository or operation responds if such a value exists.
open_points.question: If persistence contains an offset-aware timestamp, must the repository reject it as corrupt data, normalize it, or fail the affected operation with a particular boundary/domain error?
options: Reject the persisted record as invalid/corrupt and fail the operation
Normalize the value to offset-naive UTC on read without rewriting it
Normalize and repair the stored value
Permit it for compatibility despite the prohibition
open_points.default_guess: Reject the record at the persistence boundary and fail the operation without mutation.

witness.initial: A pre-existing StaffSession row contains expires_at=2026-11-06T12:00:00+00:00 rather than an offset-naive value.
events: The staff member presents that session token.
The session repository reads the row and authorization compares its expiry.
outcomes: The repository rejects the row and authentication fails because persisted data violates the clock policy.
The repository converts the timestamp to offset-naive UTC and the session authenticates normally.
witness.observer: The staff member attempting to use the session.
